audience_profile: Developers who deploy to Kubernetes but have not traced a request end to end. They know HTTP, IP addresses and containers; those are not explained.
learning_objective: After watching, the viewer can name the four decisions that route a request from the browser to a pod, in order, and knows that a Service is a name and not a running program.
creative_concept: One request is the protagonist. A single map is revealed left to right; the camera enters the AWS box as an isometric scene and the cluster as a cutaway, then pulls back to the whole map.

treatments.name: A. Follow the request
treatments.shape: One request travels through four decisions, left to right, with one misconception beat at the Service.
treatments.feasibility: Fits: CPU rendering, no paid service
treatments.verdict: Chosen. The subject is a path, so the path is the story.

treatments.name: B. Misconception throughout
treatments.shape: Open with 'the load balancer has no idea your app exists' and rebuild the true picture.
treatments.verdict: Not chosen: needs more than 60 seconds to rebuild the picture honestly. Its best beat is borrowed for the Service scene.

treatments.name: C. Failure story
treatments.shape: Trace a 502 error backwards to its cause.
treatments.verdict: Not chosen: teaches the broken path before the working one. A good sequel.

hook: You press Enter. Before the page appears, four decisions are made about where your request goes.
narrative_structure: Follow the request: hook with a count, then one scene per decision (address, node, Service, pod), a misconception beat at the Service, and a recap that returns to the opening line.
visual_direction: Three treatments, each where its form carries meaning: a 2D network-flow map as the spine; an isometric scene for the load balancer, because zones and health are spatial; a cutaway for the cluster, because it has an inside. Dark premium-technical theme, one accent colour, the request as a glowing token.
narration_approach: Calm, present tense, second person. About 150 words. One idea per sentence. Kokoro voice am_michael on the local machine.

scene_breakdown.title: Hook
scene_breakdown.purpose: State the question and the count of four

scene_breakdown.title: Service to pod
scene_breakdown.purpose: The surprise: a Service is not a program. Decision four: which pod

scene_breakdown.title: Response and recap
scene_breakdown.purpose: Return trip and the whole route in one frame

decisions.choice: Intermediate developers who deploy to Kubernetes
decisions.reason: From the brief. Basics such as what an IP address is are skipped.

decisions.choice: A concrete action plus a count: four decisions before the page appears
decisions.reason: A count gives the viewer a structure to track, and the video keeps the promise.

decisions.choice: Follow the request, with one misconception beat
decisions.reason: The path supplies the order; the misconception supplies the one surprise.

decisions.choice: 2D flow map, isometric AWS scene, Kubernetes cutaway
decisions.reason: You asked for three treatments. Each sits where its form teaches: a path as a line, zones as plates, a cluster as an opened box.

decisions.choice: Isometric projection drawn in 2D; no 3D engine
decisions.reason: Depth is only needed to show zones side by side. A flat projection renders as fast as any 2D scene on this laptop.

decisions.choice: A visual change every 2 to 4 seconds; about 150 words
decisions.reason: Dense enough for this audience, with room for the surprise to land.

decisions.choice: At the Service, two thirds through
decisions.reason: That is where attention is most likely to sag, and it is the idea most viewers hold wrongly.

decisions.choice: Return trip, then echo the opening line over the whole map
decisions.reason: Answers the opening question and leaves a frame worth pausing on.

decisions.choice: Second person, present tense, local Kokoro voice
decisions.reason: Explains as to a capable colleague; costs nothing.

decisions.choice: Local renderer, Kokoro, FFmpeg; no paid service
decisions.reason: The budget for paid services is zero and nothing here needs a GPU.

dropoff.why: Viewers who know DNS may leave.
dropoff.countermeasure: The step marker shows this is one of four.
